threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver doesn’t stop for you at the stop that doesn’t have a shelter. Welcome to Clapton, mate.
Last night on the 59, a bloke serenaded the whole bus with classic soul hits. Even the driver had to chuckle, but I swear I saw a few roll their eyes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a couple of guys having a barbecue on the sidewalk while the tram rattled by—just a regular Saturday afternoon in the hood.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop open at 3 AM, with a line of locals debating the best sauce while the nightlife hums around them.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows that the best taco trucks only show up late-night after the bars close—not during lunch. That’s prime insider knowledge.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo catching the 14, clutching a bouquet. Guessing the wedding's not in the Presidio after all.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think botigues are just for souvenirs, but they’re missing out on the best local treats—like fresh pa de coca right from the corner shop.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arriver by their overly ambitious dining choices at lunchtime—only tourists would try to snag a table at 2 PM!

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'bus stop' instead of 'the stop' like everyone else. It's a subtle shift, but it gives away your newbie status instantly.
Last week, I saw a lad on the 35 bus passionately arguing with a traffic light, insisting it was out to get him. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a pigeon stealing a slice of pizza from a street performer. It was so casual, like they both knew the hustle of this city.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can grab a döner at 4 AM and find a DJ spinning techno right next door. Only in Berlin does nightlife blend seamlessly like that.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local if they can spot a tourist trying to take an Insta pic in front of La Taqueria and chuckle as they fumble with their camera.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a saxophonist playing 'Take Five' on the 19 Polk today, mingling with the chatter. Only in SF do you get a live jazz set with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into a bar and order a 'cerveza' like it’s the same everywhere. Here, you better specify 'estrella' or 'moritz'—else you might get a blank stare.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they ask for directions to 'La Sagrada Familia' with a perfect accent, but still end up at 'La Seu' instead.
